title: Information & pseudo-filesystems
subsystem_derivation: 03 §5 (the ports — pseudo-filesystem surface). /proc and /sys are rendered as what they always morally were — computed views, now honestly derived from the record. Reads are CACHE-only reads over a computed view; their values reflect gov-os's true derived state, so byte-for-byte equality of dynamic fields is NOT promised — shape and schema are.
activation_note: This group has no single home: design/36 §6 lands the /proc files slices at EP-28 and the scheduling slices at EP-32, and names no home for the whole-system information calls (uname, sysinfo, getrusage, getrandom, syslog). Rows carry their own activates_at where the paper settles it and null where it does not; the nulls are raised, never guessed.

rows.what_it_does: Report kernel name / release / version / machine.
rows.conformance_note: Computed identity view. sysname/release fields report gov-os's true identity (a governed kernel), while the ABI struct shape is identical. Programs that gate on version strings see gov-os's honest values (03 §5).
rows.probe_absent_reason: design/36 §6 gives the /proc slices two homes — the files slices at EP-28 and the scheduling slices at EP-32 — and names no home for the whole-system information calls. This row's activation EP is therefore UNASSIGNED and is raised rather than guessed; assigning it is a plan decision, not this instrument's.

rows.what_it_does: Fill a buffer with random bytes.
rows.conformance_note: Clean INPUT case: entropy is external nondeterminism, entering the record as an input event (03 §2). This makes the draw replayable relative to the recorded input stream (03 §1.3) — determinism conditioned on the entropy being recorded, never 'free'. GRND_NONBLOCK/GRND_RANDOM, EAGAIN before pool init, blocking semantics identical.
